clue.text: Hope to nab rotten thief? Dragnet may catch one

indicators.note: to nab is to grab hold of, so the wish wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a hope is a wish

indicators.note: rotten suggests something decayed and out of shape, so the letters of thief are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hopeful policeman wants to catch a crooked thief; a police dragnet might haul one in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to nab' puts the anagram (signalled by 'rotten') inside the hope, after its first letter. The dragnet here is a fishing net, not a police sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitefish is a fish species netted commercially, and a dragnet is a fishing net hauled along the bottom.

clue.text: Squeal when I get tortured

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone under torture squeals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' rearranges WHEN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal and to whine both mean to make a high complaining cry.

clue.text: Love shown by holy man taken in by dirty cheat

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the dirty word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: dirty means impure
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A dirty swindler fools a lovesick holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' places love and the holy man together inside the dirty word, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a deception, an act of passing oneself off falsely, and a cheat in the noun sense is a fraud.

clue.text: Sixteen inadequate? Live to encompass 50, capable of more

indicators.note: inadequate suggests poor and badly formed, so the letters of sixteen are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of sixteen are taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the word for live goes round fifty

parts.note: to live is to be
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone worries that reaching sixteen is too little and hopes to live past fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' signals the anagram of the first word; 'to encompass' puts the Roman fifty inside the word for live.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extensible can be stretched or lengthened, so it is able to become larger.

clue.text: North-West Passage transport possibly motivating i.e. Cabot

indicators.note: motivating means setting in motion, so the letters of the explorer phrase are moved around

explanation.surface: An explorer named Cabot is driven to seek the North-West Passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motivating' rearranges IECABOT. John Cabot was a real explorer who sought a route to Asia, which keeps the surface tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-boat is a craft that travels on frozen water, the sort of vehicle that could cross the Arctic route.

clue.text: Wretched fellow's beheaded? Lesson that's not working

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off the word for fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: not means the word for working is missing from the lesson

parts.note: the word lesson is taken as written before the cut
something working is on

explanation.surface: A wretched man has lost his head, and a lesson has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops C from CHAP to give HAP; 'not' takes ON out of LESSON to leave LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky and unfortunate, the same sense as wretched.

clue.text: Notice Italy joining European Union? Farewell to another member!

indicators.note: joining means the pieces are put together side by side

parts.note: a notice in a paper is an advertisement, AD
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy is noticed joining the European Union, and someone says goodbye to a departing member state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to another member!' gives the surface a point about countries leaving the EU while the definition is just 'Farewell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, used in English as a formal parting word.

clue.text: Girl? One gets almost fresh

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off the word for fresh

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a girl is getting a bit cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts W from NEW to leave NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a common female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: One hard man coming up from Dublin?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word for man is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a man may be addressed as sir
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough man travels up from Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the word for man round, as fits a down clue; it sits between the one and the hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital of Ireland, so a person or thing from there is Irish.

clue.text: Presumably sharp or flat, but not produced by normal means

explanation.surface: A note that isn't natural must be sharp or flat, and is made artificially.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural is a note neither sharp nor flat, so a sharp or flat note is literally not natural; artificial things are contrary to nature.

clue.text: Computer information? 'Elpful clue about processing unit, initially

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened clue goes round the initials
the dropped H in 'Elpful shows that the word for clue loses its H too

parts.note: a clue is a hint

indicators.note: initially means take the first letters of processing and unit

explanation.surface: A helpful hint about a computer's processing unit, spoken with a dropped aitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Elpful shows a dropped aitch, telling you to drop it from the clue word too; 'about' wraps that round the initials given by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is the data fed into a computer for processing.

clue.text: What economies aim for could be inflation!

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the growth every economy wants might turn out to be inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: Economies seek growth, and inflation also means a swelling or enlarging, as of a balloon.

clue.text: A former world leader where noise is involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A former world leader was in a place where there was plenty of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' rearranges WHERE and NOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was US President from 1953 to 1961, a past head of state.

clue.text: Have a discussion if removing river from map

indicators.note: removing means taking the river letter out of the word for map

parts.note: a chart is a map

explanation.surface: People discuss whether to take a river off the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes R out of CHART.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally, a light form of conversation.

clue.text: Very old chap — that's me, so healthy, on reflection

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus, as in 'and so'

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the word for healthy is reversed

parts.note: hale means healthy

explanation.surface: An old man says he is fit and well when he thinks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns HALE into ELAH. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the Biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years, a byword for great age.

clue.text: Wind player has most of string instrument in clenched hand

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened instrument goes inside the hand

parts.note: a clenched hand is a fist

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the instrument

parts.note: the lute is a plucked string instrument

explanation.surface: A musician grips part of a stringed instrument in a tight fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last letter of the instrument; 'in' puts the rest inside the clenched hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutist plays the flute, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Suitably prepared and excited

parts.note: fit means ready or prepared, as in fit for action
tingly means thrilled and excited

explanation.surface: Someone is suitably ready and thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fittingly means appropriately, in a way that suits the occasion.

clue.text: One of Churchill's names for an overcoat

explanation.surface: Churchill gave his name to a type of overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill's full surname was Spencer-Churchill; a spencer is also a short close-fitting coat or jacket.

clue.text: Study tennis-player-one hoarding energy?

parts.note: to con is to study, an old word for learning by heart
the server is the tennis player starting a point

explanation.surface: Someone studies a tennis player who saves energy during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is a crossword staple. The definition reads a saver of energy as someone who conserves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conserver is someone who preserves or saves something, so one sparing their energy.

clue.text: Framework made from most of woody plant is ailing, pushed over

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is cut from the plant

parts.note: a tree is a woody plant

indicators.note: pushed over means toppled backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: is contracts to 's, giving S
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: A frame is built from a sick tree that has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops E from TREE; 'pushed over' turns S and ILL into LLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wood or metal supporting climbing plants.

clue.text: Composer is leading one in support

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the S goes in front

parts.note: is contracts to 's, giving S

indicators.note: in means inside, so the letter for one goes into the support

parts.note: a truss is a supporting framework or brace
a means one

explanation.surface: A composer takes the lead in supporting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts S before TRUSS, and 'in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss and Richard Strauss were famous composers.

clue.text: Alcohol-most of that's in single, knocked back

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed word for single
knocked back means turned backwards, so the word for single is reversed

parts.note: lone means single

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word that, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: Most of that drink goes into one person, who knocks it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses the word for single; 'most of' trims the last letter, and 'in' places the result after the first letter of the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the chemical name of the alcohol in drinks.

clue.text: Quote to finish up vividly clear

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
to die is to come to an end, finish

explanation.surface: An instruction to finish off a quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CITEDIE as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidetic describes mental images so detailed they are like seeing again, as with photographic memory.

clue.text: Hoist with front displaced has to move slowly

indicators.note: displaced here means knocked off, so the hoist word loses a letter

parts.note: a winch is a hoist

indicators.note: with front points to the front, the opening letter, of the hoist word as the one to go

parts.note: a winch is a hoist

explanation.surface: A hoist with a dislodged front edges along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displaced' removes the front letter of WINCH, the hoist.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to advance a tiny distance at a time.

clue.text: The best luxury car carries one upward

indicators.note: in a down clue upward means reading from the bottom up
carries means holds inside, so the car contains the letter for one

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes, a luxury car
a means one

explanation.surface: A luxury car carries one person up a hill, the finest ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts A in MERC after M, giving MAERC; 'upward' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as cream rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: In infra-red, one line is multi-coloured

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a line of descent is lineage, so line means descent

explanation.surface: Seen in infra-red light, a single line shows many colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Line as family lineage gives DESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent describes surfaces that shimmer with shifting rainbow colours.

clue.text: Sudden attack of ill-health restricts one in Italian city

indicators.note: restricts means confines inside, so the attack holds the letter for one

parts.note: a turn is a sudden bout of illness, as in having a funny turn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone falls ill suddenly while in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is British for a brief spell of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, Torino in Italian, is a major city of northern Italy.

clue.text: Remain a good person? Yes

parts.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated ST
aye, also written ay, means yes

explanation.surface: Asked whether a good person should remain, someone says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in place.

clue.text: Madly rage and mock relative

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the letters of rage are mixed up

parts.note: to mock is to taunt

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage and makes fun of a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges RAGE to GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a family member.

clue.text: City with two cathedrals lacking a mere organ

indicators.note: lacking means the city is without the pool

parts.note: Liverpool has both an Anglican and a Roman Catholic cathedral
a mere is a lake or pool

explanation.surface: A city with two cathedrals has no more than a simple organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only'; here it is a lake, POOL, removed from LIVERPOOL, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large internal organ of the body.

clue.text: Delicious last bit of saveloy gets to stomach, taking no time

indicators.note: last bit of means the final letter of saveloy
taking no means removing the letter for time from the stomach

parts.note: a tummy is a stomach

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs the last of a saveloy sausage, finding it tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a seasoned British sausage. 'taking no' removes T from TUMMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummy is an informal word for tasty.

clue.text: Bag (tea) within you want sweetener

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
char is British slang for tea
within means in

explanation.surface: A tea bag, and the offer of a sweetener in your cup.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British slang for tea. 'you want' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sugar substitute.
